newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rio Tinto farms out Wafi prospect in PNG.
newsitem.headline: Rio Tinto farms out Wafi prospect in PNG.

text.p: Australian Gold Fields NL said on Monday that it had reached an agreement with Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd for an affiliated company to earn a 45 percent stake in the Wafi gold and copper project in Papua New Guinea.
Australian Gold said its affiliate company, Provincial Gold Fields (PNG) Pty Ltd, would acquire the stake by spending US$45 million over a period of up to five years.
It said Provincial was required to spend a minimum US$15 million in the first two years and would manage the project.
Australian Gold said it currently had a 20 percent stake in Provincial, with the remainder held by unlisted United Kingdom investment group Gracechurch Plc.

The company said it would contribute to the Wafi expenditure on a pro-rata basis and had the option to raise its stake in Provincial to 60 percent at any time up to when a decision was taken to mine at Wafi.

Previous exploration at Wafi, 40 km west of Lae in the Morobe Province, had identified two large resources consisting of Zone A with inferred resources of 2.1 million ounces of gold and Zone B with total indicated and inferred resources of 1.27
million tonnes of copper and 2.0 million ounces of gold.

"The decision to farmout Wafi will free up resources to work on other projects," said Ian Gould, the managing director of Rio Tinto Australia. "Although we will not manage the Wafi program, we will maintain a majority and active interest in the project."
The Wafi project comprises three exploration licences and an application for an exploration licence with a combined area of 240 square km, Rio Tinto said.
